title: SMC Valid CHoCH vs Fake CHoCH — 4 Rules

weak_swing_point.llm_summary: Rule 1 for identifying Fake CHoCH: Weak Swing Points. A weak swing point LOOKS like a valid swing point but its strength has already been consumed because the Swing Initiating Candle (SIC) is part of a Liquidity Sweep. When the candle that creates the swing high or low is also the candle that sweeps prior liquidity, that swing point is 'weak' — its energy was used for the sweep, not for building genuine structure. If market later breaks this weak swing point, the resulting CHoCH is FAKE because the swing point was never strong to begin with. The presenter calls the candle that sweeps liquidity while creating the swing a 'Sweeping Candle.' Key identification: look at HOW the swing point was formed — if the swing-initiating candle simultaneously swept liquidity at the other end, that swing point is weak. Demonstrated on EUR/NZD 30-minute chart where weak swing points are identified and the subsequent CHoCH signals are shown to be fake.
key_rules: Weak swing point = swing where the Swing Initiating Candle is part of a Liquidity Sweep
The candle creating the swing simultaneously sweeps prior liquidity = 'Sweeping Candle'
Strength of the swing is consumed by the liquidity sweep — swing point becomes weak
Breaking a weak swing point = FAKE CHoCH (not real trend change)
Identification: check if the swing-initiating candle also swept liquidity on the other side
Weak swing points LOOK valid but are structurally exhausted
This is the most common source of fake CHoCH in real trading

engineered_liquidity_choch.llm_summary: Rule 2 for identifying Fake CHoCH: Swing Point Which Creates Engineered Liquidity. When a swing point (swing high or swing low) creates equal highs or equal lows at its level — forming engineered liquidity — then breaking that swing point does NOT constitute a real CHoCH. Instead, the break is just a liquidity sweep of the engineered liquidity zone. Smart Money creates these equal levels to trap retail traders who see 'strong support' or 'strong resistance.' When price breaks these levels, retail traders think trend has changed (CHoCH), but Smart Money is simply sweeping the accumulated orders (stop losses, buy stops, sell stops) at those engineered levels. The real move comes AFTER the sweep, in the opposite direction of what retail expects. Demonstrated on AUD/USD 4H chart showing swing points that create equal lows, which are then swept — retail sees CHoCH but it's actually fake because the swing point was an engineered liquidity zone.
key_rules: If a swing point creates equal highs or equal lows = engineered liquidity zone
Breaking a swing point that has engineered liquidity = FAKE CHoCH
The break is actually a liquidity sweep, not a real trend change
Retail traders see the equal levels as 'strong support/resistance' and get trapped
Smart Money sweeps the engineered liquidity → collects pending orders → moves opposite
Connect to V08: engineered liquidity concept (equal highs/lows are SM traps)
Must check: does the swing point have equal highs/lows around it? If yes → fake CHoCH risk

impulse_inducement_choch.llm_summary: Rule 3 for identifying Fake CHoCH: Swing High/Low Acting as Inducement. When price moves from a low to a high (or high to low) in IMPULSE form — meaning no pullback, a straight directional move — that originating low (or high) acts as inducement for the larger swing. Since the move was impulsive with no pullback, the market MUST return to that level to take inducement before the real move continues. If price breaks this level, retail traders see CHoCH, but it's actually fake because the break is simply the market taking its required inducement. The key identification is: was there any pullback between the low and the high? If NO pullback (impulse move), then the low acts as inducement and breaking it = fake CHoCH. If there WAS a pullback, the swing point is valid and breaking it could be real CHoCH. This connects to the V04 concept of inducement shift — every swing needs inducement taken before continuation.
key_rules: If price moves from low to high in IMPULSE (no pullback) → that low acts as inducement
Breaking an impulse-origin low = FAKE CHoCH (market is just taking inducement)
Impulse move = no pullback between the swing low and swing high
Market MUST return to take inducement from impulse moves — this is not trend reversal
Check: was there a pullback between low and high? No pullback = impulse = inducement level
Connects to V04 inducement shift concept: market needs inducement before continuing
The deeper the impulse move, the more likely market returns to take that inducement

multi_timeframe_hidden_trap.llm_summary: Rule 4 for identifying Fake CHoCH: Low Time Frame Swing is Higher Time Frame Inducement. This is the most advanced rule. A swing point on a lower timeframe (e.g., M15 or H1) may actually be an inducement level on a higher timeframe (e.g., H4 or D1). When the lower timeframe shows a CHoCH by breaking this swing point, it appears valid on that timeframe. But on the higher timeframe, this same level is just an inducement being taken out — not a real structure break. The higher timeframe's trend continues after taking this inducement, making the lower timeframe CHoCH fake. Traders who only look at one timeframe get trapped because they can't see that the 'structure break' on their timeframe is simply inducement collection on the higher timeframe. The presenter demonstrates on XAU/USD showing H1/M15 CHoCH indication that is actually H4/D1 inducement being taken out. The solution is multi-timeframe analysis: always check if your timeframe's swing point is a higher timeframe inducement level.
key_rules: Lower timeframe swing point can be higher timeframe inducement level
Breaking a lower TF swing that is higher TF inducement = FAKE CHoCH on lower TF
Example: M15/H1 swing low = H4/D1 inducement level → M15/H1 CHoCH is fake
Higher timeframe trend continues after taking its inducement — lower TF reversal fails
Single-timeframe traders get trapped — they can't see the higher TF inducement
Solution: always verify if your swing point is a higher TF inducement level
Multi-timeframe hierarchy: D1 > H4 > H1 > M15 — higher TF always dominates
This is the most sophisticated fake CHoCH trap — requires multi-TF analysis to detect
